From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Subject: Training on Customer Data - Opt-Out Confirmation

Alex -- thanks again for the quick call today. Wanted to summarize next steps and confirm the opt-out you requested for model training.

Recap from our call:
- Acme disclosed they will opt out of training-on-customer-data / model improvement using any Acme customer data handled by Redwood.
- Acme requires: no customer data used for model training or improvement, 90-day logs retention for request/observability, and confirmation of PII handling & data residency (US) for the pilot.
- Acme asked for a signed opt-out form and a short statement from us confirming the settings we'll enforce.

Action items for Acme (from call):
1) Confirm the person who will sign the opt-out (you mentioned security@acmeinc.com).
2) Confirm the DPA contact for redlines (legal@acmeinc.com).

Action items for Redwood:
- I'll circulate our standard training opt-out form and a written confirmation that we will not use Acme data for model improvement.
- Rishi will confirm retention and logging configuration and provide links to the SOC2 report.
- Marissa will set the account flag in our serving/runtime so model-improvement telemetry is disabled for Acme.

I've attached the training_opt_out_form.pdf for signature. Once you return the signed copy we'll apply the flag and send a formal confirmation note.

Thanks --
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: training_opt_out_form.pdf (application/pdf)

Stephanie -- thanks for the recap and quick turnaround. Confirming Acme will sign the opt-out:

- We (Acme, Inc.) opt out of Redwood using any Acme customer data for model training or model improvement.

- Data residency for the pilot should remain in the US.

I attached the signed opt-out form (signed_training_opt_out.pdf). Please confirm when the account flag is set and provide the written confirmation you mentioned. Also, our legal team will send DPA redlines to legal@redwood.ai later today.

Appreciate it --

Alex -- appreciate the quick signature. Confirming Redwood actions and constraints for the Acme pilot: 

1) Model training: we will not use any Acme customer data for model improvement or training across any of our hosted/dedicated/private modes unless Acme provides explicit written permission to opt back in. This is enforced by the account flag Marissa set.

2) Logs and retention: logs_retention_days = 90 has been created as a config for the account; infra ticket #INF-4321 tracks application of retention policy for request logs and tracing. We will not retain request-level model-improvement telemetry beyond what is necessary for 90 days.

3) PII handling & data residency: all stored artifacts for this pilot will remain in the US region. PII extraction patterns will be redacted from any debug logs unless explicitly included in a customer-provided debug bundle.

4) Documentation: Attached is the SOC2 report we shared with Marissa. For the DPA redlines, our legal team will review the doc from Acme and respond on the hubspot thread (link: https://hubspot.company/record/ACME-54).

I'll follow up once infra confirms the retention config is in place and share the final confirmation note to the security@acmeinc.com alias.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Applied ML / Inference Safety
Redwood Inference

Attachment: soc2_audit_report_2026Q2.pdf (application/pdf)
